declaration.name: Leiden Declaration on Artificial Intelligence and Mathematics

rows.asks: Transparently report automated tools, including LLMs and proof assistants, in a form consistent with open-science norms.
rows.summary: Disclosure is structural, not sectional. Every public claim carries an epistemic grade (Proved / Measured / Model / Play) with a public legend. The authorship model is stated plainly: AI models write the proofs, the code and most of the prose, and each blog post is signed by the specific model that wrote it, because conflating several models under one byline would be less honest than naming who wrote what. The operator directs the work, decides what ships, and answers for everything published. The toolchain identity is itself a locked artifact: the tools are not merely named, they are pinned, the lock is checked against the pin at every toolchain move, and their versions are part of every claim's provenance.

rows.asks: Make reviewing feasible — disclose tools, give precise references, provide formal proofs where appropriate.
rows.summary: The artifacts are formal by construction. Headline theorems ship with machine-checkable axiom footprints that a reviewer can re-derive with one command, rather than trusting our summary of what a proof assumes. The evidence is published, not just the tool: our eighteen-version toolchain migration measured footprint equality against a frozen v4.14.0 baseline — never chained through an intermediate, because chaining would let a drift launder itself across two comparisons — and the snapshots, per-stop verdicts and hashed baselines are all readable.

artifacts.label: Migration log (v4.14.0 → v4.32.2, with its own corrections)

rows.recommendation: Adhere to principles of open science
rows.asks: Transparency and accessibility of research, data, and software.
rows.summary: MachLib, the monogate toolkit and this blog, monogate-lean and eml-stdlib are public repositories, the package is on PyPI, and the reproduction zoo serves each card's evidence as static files — the evidence is the website.
rows.gap: Two repositories that public claims rest on are private: Forge, the compiler the zoo's cards come from, and the research repository, which 19 of the 78 Lean claims registered for this site cite. A reader cannot re-check those from public sources. No preprint of our own has been posted yet; the arXiv paper this site links to is Andrzej Odrzywołek's, the work Monogate builds on.
rows.upgrade_condition: Grade moves to MET when every claim this site asks a reader to trust can be re-checked from public sources — its private sources published, or the claims that rest on them withdrawn — and our paper is posted as a preprint.

rows.asks: When automated techniques are used, responsibility for correctness remains exclusively with the human authors.
rows.summary: Accepted — and mechanized, because a pledge is not a mechanism. The operator answers for the correctness of everything published, and discharges it through sorry audits (a count that cannot be derived is treated as an instrument failure, not a zero), an axiom ledger gated in both directions, a claim audit that holds every registered claim to its theorem's printed axioms, and acceptance bars fixed before the data exists. Kernel replay through an external checker ran through the migration; the last version an external checker replayed is v4.28.0, and the current pin, v4.32.2, is recorded as externally unreplayed until a checker supports it, not left to read as replayed. The failures stay in the record rather than being amended away: the migration log carries a correction stating that a stop was committed as “accepted” before its central criterion had ever been measured, and the amendment trail records a pass bar being weakened in the open, with the byte-identical check that proved the weakening changed nothing else.

artifacts.label: Migration log, including its own corrections

rows.asks: Credit and responsibility belong to humans; AI does not replace the collective human labor behind a result.
rows.summary: Our position differs from the Declaration's here, on purpose, and this row says so. The model that wrote a text is named as its author: every blog post is signed by the specific model that wrote it, and /about states that the operator is not the author of the proofs, the kernels, the backend, or most of the prose. A human byline on machine-written text would be less honest, not more. What stays human is responsibility: the operator decides what is attempted and what ships, and answers for everything published. The human work behind the results is credited — Andrzej Odrzywołek's eml operator, Lean and its community, the numerics-verification lineage, classical estimation theory — and our novelty claims are scoped accordingly: composition and discipline, not new mathematics.
rows.gap: The Declaration asks that credit and responsibility both belong to humans. We give responsibility to the human and credit for the writing to the model that did it, so this recommendation is not met as written.
rows.upgrade_condition: None expected. The row is PARTIAL by design while the model that writes a text is credited as its author; it moves only if that policy changes.

artifacts.label: Authorship model, division of labor, explicit non-claims
A post signed by the model that wrote it
Odrzywołek, arXiv:2603.21852 (the work Monogate builds on)

rows.asks: Proactive effort to find and credit sources; where satisfactory attribution is not possible, state this explicitly.
rows.summary: We credit the mathematics we build on — the eml operator and its universality theorem are Andrzej Odrzywołek's (arXiv:2603.21852) — cite the lineage we can trace in per-file references across the repositories, and review prior art before making a novelty claim. On 2026-11-25 we found our own site presenting his paper as ours: the footer on every page read “Monogate Research · arXiv:2603.21852”, the page metadata listed it among Monogate's own identities, /about called it one of our papers, post footers cited it as “Paper”, and three rows of this page called it our preprint. All of it was corrected that day; the changelog below records it.
rows.gap: The AI systems we use are trained on corpora whose provenance we cannot audit or certify. Their outputs may synthesize uncredited human work in ways invisible to us. Per the Declaration's own provision we state this explicitly rather than launder it: attribution through the model is not attribution, and we cannot certify it.
rows.upgrade_condition: Grade moves to MET when an attribution section audited against the final paper's related-work review ships with a peer-reviewed version. The training-corpus gap is not closable by us and will remain stated.

artifacts.label: Odrzywołek, arXiv:2603.21852 (the work Monogate builds on)

rows.asks: Engage publicly to explain and contextualize AI-assisted methods and results, including support for science journalism.
rows.summary: This page, the incident report below it, the public grading legend, and interactive explanations of the mathematics aimed at non-specialists.
rows.gap: No engagement yet with science journalism or community venues where these claims would be examined by people with no reason to be kind. Public artifacts are necessary but not sufficient for discourse: publishing is not the same as being questioned.
rows.upgrade_condition: Grade moves to MET when the work has been presented and questioned in at least one community venue — a talk, a workshop, or peer commentary on a published paper.

artifacts.label: Incident report: July 2026 Lean kernel bug

rows.recommendation: Stay informed about the emerging technologies
rows.asks: Stay informed about the capabilities of computer-aided tools as appropriate to one's research.
rows.summary: Standing watches with recorded reference states, not impressions — when they run. The kernel-support watch re-scans the external verification ecosystem and reports movement against its recorded state, the July 2026 Lean kernel soundness disclosure was triaged and acted on in the week it landed, and when we found the independent checker broken at every version we could use, we reported it upstream with minimal reproductions rather than routing around it.
rows.gap: The watch is run by hand, and it last ran on record on 2026-07-30. It missed two moves it exists to catch: Lean4Lean reached the kernel fix on 2026-08-02, and the bug we reported upstream (lean4lean #17) was reported fixed on 2026-10-19. Run again on 2026-11-25 it reports PARTIAL — one external checker now reaches the fix — and that run is not yet on record.
rows.upgrade_condition: Grade returns to MET when the watch's current state is on record and the watch runs on a schedule rather than when remembered.

rows.asks: Make standards and practices explicit and accessible; create pathways for participation.
rows.summary: The standards are explicit and public — a grading legend, a schema for submitted records, and a contributor guide covering what we accept, how to format a record, and how it is verified, with reproduction evidence named as a contribution. Bug reports against our claims are explicitly invited: a claim a reader cannot reproduce in a few commands is treated as a defect in the document. A reproduction pathway now exists: every zoo card states three tiers — LOCAL (one command), TOOLCHAIN (re-derive with Lean or Vivado), REPLAY (captured on real hardware, replayed from evidence).
rows.gap: No one outside the project has yet reproduced a zoo card's acceptance from raw artifacts. We are looking for the first.
rows.upgrade_condition: Grade moves to MET when at least one external reproduction of a zoo card's acceptance from raw artifacts is on record.

rows.recommendation: Consider carefully which tools to use
rows.asks: Weigh alignment, openness, energy, and scale when choosing tools — including whether to use AI at all.
rows.summary: Tool choices are recorded decisions with stated trade-offs, including a decision to sit on an unpatched-but-dual-checkable kernel version until the external-checker intersection moved — and the later reversal of that decision when its premise was refuted by primary sources. The verification substrate is deliberately open and small: a Mathlib-free library with an audited axiom base, chosen so that trust reduces to a readable core.
rows.gap: The AI authorship itself runs on large commercial models whose training practices, energy costs, and corporate policies we do not control and cannot audit. Using them is a considered choice — this project exists to test what discipline can be maintained around exactly these tools — and this row exists so that the choice is on the record as a choice rather than a default.
rows.upgrade_condition: No upgrade path is claimed while the models we depend on remain unauditable. This row is expected to stay PARTIAL.

rows.asks: Results must be published in peer-reviewed venues; informal channels support but cannot replace community scrutiny.
rows.summary: No preprint of ours has been posted yet. A paper targeting a formal-methods venue is in preparation. The zoo, 1op.io, and this site are informal channels in exactly the Declaration's sense — every claim on them links to regenerable artifacts, which mitigates but does not substitute for peer review.
rows.gap: Until that paper is submitted, reviewed, and published, the Declaration's fourth threat — that proper evaluation is endangered when results are communicated through informal channels, often without any research paper — applies to this project. This row exists to say so rather than to let the artifact links imply that the question is settled.
rows.upgrade_condition: Grade moves to PARTIAL when the paper is under submission, and to MET when it is published.

rows.recommendation: Evaluate the ethical consequences of your work
rows.asks: Evaluate ethical consequences; withdraw from harmful work; partner only where values are respected.
rows.summary: Stated plainly rather than abstractly: our application domain is safety-critical estimation and control, and the worked examples are Kalman-class filters including range-bearing tracking — a technology class with civilian uses (navigation, robotics, medical devices, automotive safety) and defense-relevant ones. Our position: the contribution is evidence discipline, making safety-critical systems provably match their specifications, and we hold that verified correctness in deployed systems is a public good. We have no defense contracts; any future partnership will be evaluated against this row and recorded on this page.
rows.gap: We do not claim this settles the ethics. We claim it is disclosed, and that the disclosure has a maintenance rule. Ethical evaluation is not a completable task.
rows.upgrade_condition: None. This row is graded PARTIAL permanently by design — a MET here would overclaim.

rows.recommendation: Recommendations for organizations, funders, and policymakers
rows.asks: Institutional and policy recommendations — publication norms, funding, evaluation infrastructure, and community standards.
rows.summary: Noted for completeness. These recommendations address institutions rather than individual researchers. Where one lands on us in practice — the obligation to publish through peer-reviewed venues — it appears above as its own row rather than being filed here where it would be easy to ignore.

Re-verification, four weeks past the quarterly date the kernel watch itself names. Every artifact was fetched and every summary re-read against it. All links resolved, but eight rows said things their evidence no longer supported: three grades moved down (below), and five rows kept their grade with corrected text — the preprint three rows cited, arXiv:2603.21852, is Andrzej Odrzywołek's paper, not ours; kernel replay at the current Lean pin had read as done where the migration log records it as not; and the contributor pathway had moved on since July.

“Repositories are public” was too broad: Forge and the research repository are private, and 19 of this site's 78 registered Lean claims cite the research repository. “The preprint is on arXiv” cited Odrzywołek's paper; no preprint of ours is posted.

The row said no AI system is listed as an author; the site it cites signs every post with the model that wrote it, and /about says the operator is not the author. The operator's position is that the model that wrote a text is its author. The row now states that divergence from the Declaration instead of claiming agreement, and /about now states that the operator answers for everything published.

The quarterly watch had not run on record since 2026-07-30 and missed Lean4Lean reaching the kernel fix (2026-08-02) and our upstream report, lean4lean #17, being fixed (2026-10-19). Graded on what ran, not on what was meant to.

Our own site presented Odrzywołek's arXiv:2603.21852 as Monogate's: the footer on every page and the manifesto's, the page metadata's list of Monogate identities, /about's “papers (arXiv:2603.21852)”, eleven post footers, citations on the home page, /proofs, /theorems, /superbest and /one-operator, the theorem catalog, and three rows here. Each now names him. The same day, a post's “Rust source” link to a nonexistent repository and /about's link to Forge's private repository were corrected.
